report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary

The application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations under the EU AI Act has shifted since the Act's original enactment. As originally passed in 2024, these obligations were set to apply from **2 August 2026**, but following the "AI Omnibus" amendment to Article 113, the current officially confirmed application date is **2 December 2027**, with a separate extension to **2 August 2028** for high-risk systems embedded as safety components in Annex I products (high confidence). Unverified claims of a further extension to 2 August 2029 appear in low-authority sources and are not corroborated by any official EU institution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Enactment)
As enacted in 2024, the AI Act's high-risk rules, including Annex III obligations, were originally scheduled to apply from **2 August 2026** [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence) (high confidence). A 2023-era European Parliament summary also described high-risk obligations as applying 36 months after entry into force, placing this around August 2027 [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence) (medium confidence). A 2024 Goodwin commentary, predating the Omnibus amendments, described full high-risk compliance as expected "by 2027" (low confidence) [Goodwin](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Digital Omnibus on AI amended Article 113 to extend the Annex III high-risk application date to **2 December 2027** [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (high confidence). The same amendment extended the application date for high-risk systems embedded as safety components in Annex I products to **2 August 2028** [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf) (high confidence). Article 113 as amended specifies that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III obligations), except Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) [ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). Procedurally, the Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, a political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026 [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules) (high confidence).

### Interpretive and Transitional Notes
A consolidated EUR-Lex text and Article 111 guidance still reference 2 August 2026 as "the date of application of Chapter III" for determining when already-placed systems become subject to rules only upon significant design changes, which may reflect legacy drafting language rather than the current compliance deadline (high confidence) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111). Commentary prior to the Omnibus taking effect noted that if the amendments had not been approved before 2 August 2026, the original high-risk provisions would have applied by default, making 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 "backstop dates" contingent on adoption (low confidence) [LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO). Separately, Annex III itself lists eight categories of AI use cases that *may* be classified as high-risk, rather than an automatic list of high-risk systems (low confidence) [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2).

### Disputed Further Extension
Some sources report a further amendment, allegedly occurring in September 2026, moving the Annex III application date from 2 December 2027 to **2 August 2029** (high confidence rating assigned by corroboration count, but sourced entirely from unverifiable domains) [example legal guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update). This claim is not supported by any official EU source in this dataset.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Several news/blog sources (Responsible AI Labs, McKenna Consultants, Cloud Security Alliance) still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline without acknowledging the Omnibus amendment, conflicting with official EU guidance confirming 2 December 2027. Given the recency and authority of EU Commission and Council sources, 2 December 2027 is better supported. The claimed 2029 extension (flagged above, confidence 0.70 by corroboration metric) is sourced only from domains with ".example" suffixes, suggesting these may be placeholder, fabricated, or unverifiable sources rather than legitimate legal reporting; this claim should be treated with significant skepticism despite its later publication dates.

## Knowledge Gaps

It remains unclear whether the alleged 2 August 2029 extension is a real legal development, as no Official Journal or EUR-Lex citation has been identified. It is also unclear whether EUR-Lex's consolidated text and Article 111 guidance have been fully updated to reflect the Omnibus changes, given lingering references to 2 August 2026. Further research is needed on whether sub-deadlines exist for different Annex III use-case categories, and how the "significant design change" rule for legacy systems interacts with the new 2027/2028 dates.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary

The application date for Annex III high-risk AI system obligations under the EU AI Act has shifted since the Act's original enactment. As originally passed in 2024, these obligations were set to apply from **2 August 2026**, but following the "AI Omnibus" amendment to Article 113, the current officially confirmed application date is **2 December 2027**, with a separate extension to **2 August 2028** for high-risk systems embedded as safety components in Annex I products (high confidence). Unverified claims of a further extension to 2 August 2029 appear in low-authority sources and are not corroborated by any official EU institution.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (2024 Enactment)
As enacted in 2024, the AI Act's high-risk rules, including Annex III obligations, were originally scheduled to apply from **2 August 2026** [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence) (high confidence). A 2023-era European Parliament summary also described high-risk obligations as applying 36 months after entry into force, placing this around August 2027 [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence) (medium confidence). A 2024 Goodwin commentary, predating the Omnibus amendments, described full high-risk compliance as expected "by 2027" (low confidence) [Goodwin](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The Digital Omnibus on AI amended Article 113 to extend the Annex III high-risk application date to **2 December 2027** [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force) (high confidence). The same amendment extended the application date for high-risk systems embedded as safety components in Annex I products to **2 August 2028** [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf) (high confidence). Article 113 as amended specifies that Chapter III, Sections 1–3 (covering Annex III obligations), except Article 6(5), apply from 2 December 2027 (medium confidence) [ai-act-law.eu](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113). Procedurally, the Omnibus proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, a political agreement was reached on 7 May 2026, and it entered into force on 27 July 2026 [European Commission](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules) (high confidence).

### Interpretive and Transitional Notes
A consolidated EUR-Lex text and Article 111 guidance still reference 2 August 2026 as "the date of application of Chapter III" for determining when already-placed systems become subject to rules only upon significant design changes, which may reflect legacy drafting language rather than the current compliance deadline (high confidence) [EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111). Commentary prior to the Omnibus taking effect noted that if the amendments had not been approved before 2 August 2026, the original high-risk provisions would have applied by default, making 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 "backstop dates" contingent on adoption (low confidence) [LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO). Separately, Annex III itself lists eight categories of AI use cases that *may* be classified as high-risk, rather than an automatic list of high-risk systems (low confidence) [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2).

### Disputed Further Extension
Some sources report a further amendment, allegedly occurring in September 2026, moving the Annex III application date from 2 December 2027 to **2 August 2029** (high confidence rating assigned by corroboration count, but sourced entirely from unverifiable domains) [example legal guide](https://eu-ai-act-legal-guide.example/2026/09/15/annex-iii-deadline-update). This claim is not supported by any official EU source in this dataset.

## Contradictions & Uncertainties

Several news/blog sources (Responsible AI Labs, McKenna Consultants, Cloud Security Alliance) still cite 2 August 2026 as the operative deadline without acknowledging the Omnibus amendment, conflicting with official EU guidance confirming 2 December 2027. Given the recency and authority of EU Commission and Council sources, 2 December 2027 is better supported. The claimed 2029 extension (flagged above, confidence 0.70 by corroboration metric) is sourced only from domains with ".example" suffixes, suggesting these may be placeholder, fabricated, or unverifiable sources rather than legitimate legal reporting; this claim should be treated with significant skepticism despite its later publication dates.

## Knowledge Gaps

It remains unclear whether the alleged 2 August 2029 extension is a real legal development, as no Official Journal or EUR-Lex citation has been identified. It is also unclear whether EUR-Lex's consolidated text and Article 111 guidance have been fully updated to reflect the Omnibus changes, given lingering references to 2 August 2026. Further research is needed on whether sub-deadlines exist for different Annex III use-case categories, and how the "significant design change" rule for legacy systems interacts with the new 2027/2028 dates.
